purpose: The commander's test of the agent body (8a05299): a teammate spawned from a session launched on the body answers as crew, carries no session start duty, and does not hold the pilot's body in its system prompt
roster_note: no roster; one cheap test seat

seats.name: body-tester
seats.reason: a fresh Haiku teammate that reads one cockpit file and reports who it is, whether it has a session start duty, and what its system prompt opens with
seats.returns: answers a to d by SendMessage, under 200 words

shape: one teammate, one brief, one follow-up if needed; the pilot checks the self-report against the teammate's transcript on disk (rule 4)
scope: body-tester reads only the cockpit README.md and writes nothing
outcome: Passed. body-tester answered crew, no session start duty, and no pilot body, identity or commander dossier in its prompt. Verified by the pilot on disk: the teammate's transcript under the session's subagents folder carries prompt_snapshot rows holding its system prompt, with zero matches for pilot, commander or cockpit. The cockpit CLAUDE.md reached it as a nested_memory attachment, not in the system prompt as it claimed. Report in records/notepad/agent-body-2026-09-20/teammate-test-2026-09-21.md. Open: whether the failed read or the cockpit working directory triggered the CLAUDE.md load; initialPrompt on resume is the commander's remaining test.
lessons: a teammate's system prompt is on disk in the prompt_snapshot rows of its transcript; read it instead of asking the teammate
the brief named a cockpit root README.md that does not exist; glance at a path before briefing it
search the transcript for strings the brief does not contain, or the brief's own text counts as matches
the pilot's shell directory at spawn becomes the teammate's working directory
